text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Zambia Democratic Congress (ZDC) has expelled its two vice presidents and treasurer for criticising party president Dean Mungomba's call for an armed insurrection to unseat the government.
- Norway has signed an agreement under which it will release 250 million kroner in project assistance to Zambia.
- A Zambia Air Force plane has crash landed on a busy highway outside the capital after developing a mechanical fault. There were no casualties.

- A traditional ruler in southern Zambia has threatened his subjects with police action for refusing to incorporate programmes of the opposition United National Independece Party (UNIP) in their areas.
- Zambian information minister David Mpamba has proposed a media programme exchange between Zambia and Malawi to narrow the language barrier between the two countries.
- The police were called in to disperse over 500 retrenched tax office workers who planned a protest outside the Ministry of Finance over non-payment of benefits.
